tools.name: datadog_search_logs
tools.description: Search Datadog logs and return matching entries as compact text. Best for pinpoint lookups: a known query, a few rows, one attribute to check. For broad investigation (unknown error shape, need volume/timeline/breakdowns) use datadog_run_investigation instead — one call fetches rows+timeline+facets+patterns into a server-side session that datadog_get_session_logs can drill into without further Datadog calls. For a visual, user-facing investigation use datadog_investigate_logs.

query.description: Datadog logs search query, e.g. "service:payments status:error". Note: free-text terms only match the log message, not custom attributes — to match inside an attribute use its @path, e.g. @error:*SomeException*.

from.description: Start time: Datadog time math ("now-4h") or ISO 8601 with a time zone (Z or offset)

to.description: End time: Datadog time math ("now") or ISO 8601 with a time zone (Z or offset)

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous result

attributes.description: Log attribute keys to append to each line as key=value, looked up by dot path in the log's custom attributes. JSON array, e.g. ["http.status_code", "error.kind"] (a comma-separated string also works). Missing keys are skipped. Values over 300 chars are middle-truncated; for full values run datadog_run_investigation and use datadog_get_session_logs detail mode.

dedupe.description: Cluster the fetched page into message patterns and return one line per pattern (count + template + example) instead of one line per log. Applies to the fetched page only (up to limit rows).

tools.name: datadog_aggregate_logs
tools.description: Count Datadog logs grouped by a facet (e.g. service, status, host, @http.status_code), or as a timeseries when interval is set. Returns a text table for model-side analysis.

from.description: Start time: Datadog time math or ISO 8601 with a time zone (Z or offset)

to.description: End time: time math or ISO 8601 with a time zone (Z or offset)

groupBy.description: Facet to group by, e.g. "service", "status", "host", "@http.status_code". Defaults to "status".

interval.description: When set (e.g. "5m", "1h"), returns a timeseries of counts instead of totals

tools.name: datadog_get_trace
tools.description: Fetch all APM spans of one trace by trace_id and render them as a chronological parent/child tree with service, resource, span type, start offset, duration, and error markers. Use it to pivot from a log line's trace_id=... field (shown in datadog_search_logs output) into the distributed trace behind it. Set from/to so the range brackets the log's timestamp (e.g. 30 minutes either side). For large traces prefer errors_only=true or a small max_spans to keep the output focused.

trace_id.description: APM trace ID, e.g. the trace_id=... value on a datadog_search_logs line

from.description: Start time bracketing the trace: Datadog time math ("now-4h") or ISO 8601 with a time zone

to.description: End time: Datadog time math ("now") or ISO 8601 with a time zone (Z or offset)

errors_only.description: Render only error spans and their ancestor chains; other spans are counted, not listed

collapse.description: Collapse runs of identical leaf sibling spans (same service/resource/type) into one xN line

tools.name: datadog_search_events
tools.description: Search Datadog events (deployments, monitor alerts, config changes, custom events) and return them as compact chronological text. Use it to correlate an error window found in logs with what changed: e.g. query "source:github tags:service:web" for deployment events around the incident, or "source:alert" for monitor transitions. Supports Datadog events search syntax.

query.description: Datadog events search query, e.g. "source:github tags:service:web" for deployments of a service

from.description: Start time: Datadog time math ("now-1d") or ISO 8601 with a time zone (Z or offset)

to.description: End time: Datadog time math ("now") or ISO 8601 with a time zone (Z or offset)

max_tags.description: Max tags per event line; 0 hides tags for a pure timeline

tools.name: datadog_query_metrics
tools.description: Query Datadog metric timeseries with the classic metric query syntax and return compact per-series stats plus downsampled values. Use it to correlate resource/latency behavior with a log error window: e.g. "avg:system.cpu.user{service:web} by {host}", "avg:trace.express.request.duration{service:api}", "sum:trace.express.request.errors{service:api}.as_count()".

from.description: Start time: Datadog time math ("now-1h") or ISO 8601 with a time zone (Z or offset)

to.description: End time: Datadog time math ("now") or ISO 8601 with a time zone (Z or offset)

max_series.description: Max series to return for group-by queries (highest average first)

tools.name: datadog_run_investigation
tools.description: Run a log investigation (log page + status timeline + facet breakdowns) WITHOUT opening a UI. The full result is stored server-side under a viewUUID; only a compact summary is returned. Pass the same viewUUID to iterate on one session (refine the query, or load more rows with cursor), then call datadog_investigate_logs with the viewUUID to display the session to the user. Sessions are cached in memory and mirrored to disk, so a viewUUID usually survives server restarts.

query.description: Datadog logs search query (default: "*"; inherited when continuing with viewUUID + cursor)

from.description: Start time: Datadog time math or ISO 8601 (default: "now-1h"; inherited for cursor continuation)

to.description: End time (default: "now"; inherited for cursor continuation)

groupBy.description: Extra facet to break down by, e.g. "@http.status_code"

limit.description: Max log rows to fetch and store in the session (not returned to you)

viewUUID.description: Existing investigation session to update/iterate on; omit to create a new one

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous summary — appends the next page of rows (requires viewUUID)

sampleRows.description: How many sample log lines to include in the summary

findings.description: Plain-text findings/notes to attach to the session; shown in the UI and HTML report. Replaces previous findings.

title.description: Human-readable title for this investigation / report

includeEvents.description: Also fetch Datadog events (deploys, alerts) in the window and overlay them on the timeline (default true)

eventsQuery.description: Events search query, e.g. "source:github tags:service:web" (default: all events in the window)

metricsQueries.description: Metric queries to fetch alongside logs (classic syntax), e.g. ["avg:system.cpu.user{service:web}", "avg:trace.express.request.duration{service:web}"]

tools.name: datadog_get_session_logs
tools.description: Read log rows already stored in a datadog_run_investigation session — no Datadog API call, no rate cost. List mode (default): compact one-line-per-log output filtered by status/service/pattern/contains with offset/limit paging. Detail mode: pass logId or row to get one full raw log as JSON (use fields to select attribute paths on large logs). Pattern numbers (#1…) and row indexes ([N]) come from the datadog_run_investigation summary and from list output; row indexes stay valid across cursor load-more but reset when the session query is re-run.

logId.description: Detail mode: full log ID — returns the complete raw log as JSON

row.description: Detail mode: stored row index (the [N] prefix in list output) — alternative to logId

fields.description: Detail mode: attribute dot-paths to return instead of the full JSON (for large logs). JSON array or comma-separated string.

status.description: List filter: only these statuses, e.g. ["error","warn"] (or "error,warn")

pattern.description: List filter: rows matching pattern #N from the summary (1-based)

contains.description: List filter: case-insensitive substring of the message

offset.description: List mode: rows to skip (for paging)

limit.description: List mode: max rows to return

attributes.description: List mode: attribute dot-paths appended per line as key=value, looked up in the stored raw log. JSON array, e.g. ["http.status_code", "error.kind"] (a comma-separated string also works). Missing keys are skipped; long values are middle-truncated — use detail mode for full values.

tools.name: datadog_export_report
tools.description: Export an investigation session to the export directory, WITHOUT opening a UI. Pass the viewUUID returned by datadog_run_investigation or datadog_investigate_logs. format "html" (default) writes a self-contained report with the timeline chart, facet breakdowns, message patterns, log entries and any findings, and opens it in the default browser when possible. format "csv" or "json" writes the fetched log rows as data instead (not opened automatically) — share the saved path with the user.

viewUUID.description: Investigation view ID from a previous investigation tool result

format.description: Output format: "html" report (default), or "csv"/"json" of the fetched log rows

tools.name: datadog_investigate_logs
tools.description: Open an interactive Datadog log investigation UI (timeline chart, facet breakdowns, log table). The user can adjust the query/time range in the UI and export a shareable HTML report. Returns a viewUUID and a summary. Pass a viewUUID from datadog_run_investigation to display an already-investigated session without re-fetching. For plain text results use datadog_search_logs.

query.description: Datadog logs search query, e.g. "service:payments status:error"

from.description: Start time: Datadog time math ("now-4h") or ISO 8601

groupBy.description: Extra facet to break down by, e.g. "@http.status_code"

title.description: Human-readable title for this investigation / report

viewUUID.description: Display an existing investigation session (from datadog_run_investigation) instead of running a new query. Other query params are ignored when the session exists.

findings.description: Plain-text findings/notes to show in the UI findings panel and HTML report

includeEvents.description: Also fetch Datadog events (deploys, alerts) in the window and overlay them on the timeline (default true)

eventsQuery.description: Events search query, e.g. "source:github tags:service:web" (default: all events in the window)

metricsQueries.description: Metric queries to show alongside logs (classic syntax), e.g. ["avg:system.cpu.user{service:web}"]

tools.name: _get_view_state
tools.description: Fetch the stored investigation result for a viewUUID. Only callable from the app UI.

viewUUID.description: Investigation view ID from the tool result text

tools.name: _run_investigation
tools.description: Re-run the investigation with adjusted parameters and update the stored view state. Only callable from the app UI.

from.description: Start time (Datadog time math or ISO 8601)

groupBy.description: Extra facet to break down by

cursor.description: Pagination cursor — appends the next page of rows to the view

includeEvents.description: Fetch Datadog events for the window (inherited when omitted)

metricsQueries.description: Metric queries to fetch alongside logs (inherited when omitted)

tools.name: _get_log_detail
tools.description: Fetch the full raw log event for a row in the investigation table. Only callable from the app UI.

tools.name: _export_report
tools.description: Export the investigation to the export directory as an HTML report (default) or CSV/JSON of the fetched rows. Only callable from the app UI.

rowIds.description: csv/json only: export just these stored rows (e.g. the filtered view)
